name: Invesco Short Duration US Government Securities Fund
oneLiner: USTB is Invesco's tokenized short-duration Treasury fund, managed by Invesco Advisers on Superstate infrastructure for accredited investors.
collateral: Short-duration U.S. Treasury bills held by The Bank of New York Mellon, with holdings disclosed publicly and liquidity available each market day; managed by Invesco Advisers, Inc.
pegMechanism: NAV-accreting fund share token (not pegged to $1); price launched at ~$10/share and appreciates continuously as Treasury income accrues; subscription and redemption at daily NAV in USDC or USD; NAV calculated by NAV Fund Services each NYSE/Federal Reserve business day

proofOfReserves.provider: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (fund auditor); public holdings and on-chain NAV provide daily transparency
proofOfReserves.attestorLicense: SEC-exempt private fund (Reg D Rule 506(c) / ICA §3(c)(7))

jurisdiction.license: Reg D Rule 506(c); Delaware Statutory Trust; restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers and Accredited Investors

applicabilityBasis.summary: USTB is a Section 3(c)(7) private investment fund offering tokenized shares in a short-duration U.S. Treasury fund; it meets the definition of a security under federal securities laws and is expressly excluded from the GENIUS Act definition of a payment stablecoin (which excludes any asset that otherwise qualifies as a security under the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Company Act of 1940, or the Investment Advisers Act of 1940). USTB is not marketed or used as a payment instrument; its token represents a fund share that accretes at NAV.

genius.issuerEntity: Superstate Trust (d/b/a Invesco Short-Duration U.S. Government Securities Fund after the completed Invesco takeover in Q2 2026)
genius.licensingRegulator: SEC — private Section 3(c)(7) fund exempt from Investment Company Act registration; offered under Reg D Rule 506(c); N-1A pending for conversion to registered MMF
genius.notes: USTB is outside GENIUS payment-stablecoin tracking because it is a tokenized fund share (security), not a payment stablecoin. Invesco completed the takeover in Q2 2026; the token addresses, smart contracts, and USTB ticker will remain unchanged. A pending N-1A before the SEC (filed April 2025) would convert the fund to a registered money market fund upon reorganization — this would not change the excluded-security classification.

review.evidence: At block 25294990: owner() = 0xad309BB6f13074128b4F23EF9EA2fe8552AfCA83, eth_getCode = '0x' (EOA confirmed). ProxyAdmin owner() = same address. Token and ProxyAdmin both confirmed under same issuer EOA. No on-chain roles beyond owner; issuance is issuer-backend via Superstate's fund subscription API. Economic-control evidence reviewed 2026-07-15: NAV Fund Services independently calculates recurring USTB NAV and PwC audits the fund; the current product page exposes continuous NAV per share. The same page states that the fund is not registered under the Investment Company Act, and its Rule 506(c)/Section 3(c)(7) filing is not prudential supervision. 2026-07-20 follow-up: the token is a transparent proxy (EIP-1967 implementation 0x1f50a1ee0ec8275d0c83b7bb08896b4b47d6e8c4, admin 0xb9d285dcad879513dc9c1a3b2e0cccb21c3c2146) whose ProxyAdmin owner() = 0xad309bb6f13074128b4f23ef9ea2fe8552afca83, matching the reviewed control; the proxy admin can change mint-critical logic with no on-chain delay.
